subject: Headwind first-capture: hmdm boots clean but admin/admin gets 401 — the seeded admin password is not 'admin'. No patch applied, per your note.
body:
Capturing the failure rather than patching around it, as your request's second note directed. This is NOT the JWT login-shape mismatch you anticipated — the endpoint and body shape are correct. It is a credential mismatch, and hmdm comes up perfectly healthy.

RAN at 6205a55, clean tree:
  live-headwind     REFUSED_MISSING_PREREQUISITE (429s) — lane SKIPPED, no capture minted
  proofs-sim-only   PASS (5s)

The runner did the right thing: SKIP, not FAIL, 'a skipped lane proved nothing', request stays open. Result committed.

WHY IT SKIPPED. The container is fully up — Liquibase migrations complete, 'Application initialization was successful', ActiveMQ started, Tomcat 'Server startup in 36128 ms', http-nio-8080 listening. The war dance was never needed; the war shipped in the image. Health never went green solely because the readiness probe authenticates, and the login is rejected:

  POST http://127.0.0.1:8425/rest/public/jwt/login  {"login":"admin","password":"admin"}
  -> HTTP 401 Unauthorized (Tomcat error page, not a JSON body)
  audit log inside the container: action='plugin.audit.action.jwt.login', login='admin', errorCode='2'

errorCode=2 on this build is bad-credentials, not a missing user. The user row exists:

  select login, password from users where login='admin';
  -> admin | 349242D38ED8667B5C11D2412EBEA4636BD3CA3A

That stored hash is neither sha1('admin') (d033e22ae348aeb5660fc2140aec35850c4da997) nor md5('admin') (21232f297a57a5a743894a0e4a801fc3). hmdm salts the admin password, so the DB ships a pre-seeded admin whose cleartext is NOT 'admin'. run-live-lanes.sh:373 and :390 both send admin/admin, so the probe can never reach 200 and the JWT for the capture step is never minted.

WHERE I THINK THE WIRES CROSSED. Your note said the NPE was pre-empted by 'setting the config password before the proof runs'. That is the CONFIGURATION shared-secret (configurations table), a different thing from the admin USER password (users table). Setting the former does not change the latter, and the login uses the latter.

FIX OPTIONS, none applied — your call which is right:
  (a) Reset the admin hash in Postgres to a known value during bring-up, right after the container is healthy and before the probe — e.g. UPDATE users SET password=<hmdm's own salted hash of a known pw> WHERE login='admin'. Needs hmdm's exact hashing (salt source), so it is their algorithm, not a guess.
  (b) Find the actual seeded default for hmdm 0.1.5 / 5.30.3-os and use it — if the image documents one.
  (c) Have bring-up create a fresh admin via hmdm's own init/CLI rather than relying on the seed.

I did not brute-force the password — a credential-guessing loop is both the wrong move and blocked by policy here. Containers were kept only long enough to read the logs and the users row, then removed; nothing is left running. Ready to test whichever fix you land, on this Mac, the moment it is on the branch.
